clue.text: Excellent meal, but requiring no repetition

indicators.note: the meal's name has a letter said twice in a row, and a thing that needs no repeating keeps only one of them

explanation.surface: A diner praises a meal but asks not to be served the same thing twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent meal' reads as one phrase, but the split comes straight after 'Excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: super is informal British praise, as in 'a super idea'.

clue.text: Party in charge in Asian country after uprising

indicators.note: the charge abbreviation is placed in the middle of the country's name
an uprising goes upward, and in a down clue going up means reading the letters bottom to top

explanation.surface: A political party takes power in an Asian country after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political, and 'uprising' backs that up; but the party is a get-together and the uprising flips the country with its new passenger inside, so the charge letters read backwards too.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a social is an informal gathering, like a church or club social evening.

clue.text: Request certain suggestions about river journeys offering a good time

indicators.note: 'about' as in 'round about': the suggestions are placed around the river letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks for firm ideas about which river cruises will be fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River journeys' looks like one phrase, but 'river' belongs to the wordplay and the definition starts at 'journeys'.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase: pleasure trips are outings taken purely for enjoyment rather than business.

clue.text: Profligate vacation’s ending in French city

indicators.note: a word's ending is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a roué is a dissolute man, a rake

explanation.surface: A spendthrift finishes his holiday in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profligate' is an adjective in the surface but has to be read as a noun, the rake himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Rouen is the historic capital of Normandy, on the Seine.

clue.text: Money received of those people, having acquired a promenade?

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it in, so the pronoun takes the A inside itself

blocks.note: the take is the money taken in, as at a box office
the article, used as a letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a group earned after they got hold of a seafront promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A promenade' looks like a noun phrase, but the A is swallowed by THEIR and 'promenade' is a verb, to stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense: to promenade is to stroll for pleasure and fresh air, the old idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Rocker’s equivalent to this roller?

blocks.note: the word that can replace 'rocker' in 'off one's rocker', meaning mad
a wheeled cart for shopping or luggage

explanation.surface: A question comparing something that rocks with something that rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: The link is an idiom: someone crazy is 'off their rocker', or equally 'off' the answer, so in that phrase the two words swap freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an idiom partner for rocker in phrases meaning mad, and a wheeled cart that rolls.

clue.text: Delivery chap who’s peckish?

blocks.note: reads as a courier or postman; he delivers greetings in person
reads as hungry; really, given to pecks, little kisses

explanation.surface: A delivery man who is feeling hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peckish' normally means a bit hungry; here it means given to pecks, the little kisses this messenger delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: a kissogram is a greeting delivered in person with a kiss, so its courier deals in pecks.

clue.text: It’s provocative carrying stone clubs, for example

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the provocative word holds the stone and clubs letters inside

blocks.note: a tease is someone or something provocative

explanation.surface: Something provocative is carried by stone-age clubs, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone clubs' suggests cavemen, but it is two abbreviations; a stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a test case is an example whose outcome sets the pattern for others.

clue.text: Prepare Parisian who will cut recording

indicators.note: to cut something is to slice into it, so the French word lands in the middle of the record

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Get ready the Parisian who will edit a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' is the usual signal to translate the next word into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to equip someone is to fit them out, getting them ready.

clue.text: To sum up about computers etc, lately disheartened to a great extent

indicators.note: 'about' as in 'around': the summing-up phrase goes around the computers abbreviation
the heart of a word is its middle, so a disheartened word keeps only its ends

blocks.note: in fine is a formal phrase meaning finally, in summary
the first and last letters of lately

explanation.surface: A summary of how computers have lately become far more dispiriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fine' is an old Latin-derived phrase for 'in short', rare outside crosswords and legal prose.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase of degree: infinitely, used loosely, means immensely, as in 'infinitely better'.

clue.text: Learned person positioned to accept leading figures

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the seated word takes the front-runners inside

blocks.note: the van is the vanguard, the people at the front

explanation.surface: A scholar is placed to receive the most important people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading figures' looks like VIPs; here it is the van, the front of an army or movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: savant is French for a learned person, a scholar of deep knowledge.

clue.text: American President initially has reduced chilly reception, being unable to make speech?

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the opening letters of American President count
a reduced word has been cut down, here losing its final letter

blocks.note: a chilly reception is ice, cut short

explanation.surface: An American president given a frosty welcome is lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a president too offended to speak; the question mark marks the definition as a playful paraphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term: aphasia is loss of the power to produce or understand language, often after a stroke.

clue.text: A passion arising in celebrity circus performer

indicators.note: something arising goes up, and in a down clue going up means reading bottom to top
the upturned piece is placed inside the celebrity word

blocks.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A craze rising among the famous for a circus act.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion point is just after the first letter of the celebrity word, which is easy to miss because both pieces begin with A.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: an aerialist performs high in the air, on trapeze or tightrope.

clue.text: Impressive tango? Rash going topless

indicators.note: losing one's top; in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Tango is T in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone praises a daring tango, or warns against rashly stripping off.
explanation.walkthrough: Tasty for impressive is British slang, as in a tasty goal or a tasty line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang sense: tasty describes something formidable or admirable, like a tasty line-up.

clue.text: Comedy film that’ll have you thinking of better activities?

definitions.text: Comedy film that’ll have you thinking of better activities?

blocks.note: a straight description: the title of a film comedy

blocks.clueFragment: that’ll have you thinking of better activities?
blocks.note: reads as preferring other pastimes; really, the activities of a better, one who bets

explanation.surface: A film so dull it makes you wish you were doing something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as more pleasant; it is one who bets, so the activities are wagers on horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A title with a pun: the 1937 Marx Brothers comedy is set around a racetrack full of gamblers.

clue.text: Ready to accept unimaginative cut in revised course

indicators.note: a cut word has been trimmed, here losing its final letter
the trimmed word is placed inside the rearranged one
a revised text has been reworked, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A college is ready to accept cuts to a course that was too dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the thing being accepted; it only shortens the unimaginative word.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: credulous people are too ready to accept what they are told, lacking scepticism.

clue.text: Duffers upset with this society after time, old fogeys

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Incompetents annoyed with a club after a while: stuffy old men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like an order instruction, but everything is mixed together, so it only adds the time letter to the pile.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a stuffed shirt is a pompous, old-fashioned person, much like a fogey.

clue.text: Club second to enter sports venue beside lake

indicators.note: to enter a place is to go inside it, so the second goes inside the venue
beside means next to, so the lake letter is added on after

blocks.note: an arena is a sports venue

explanation.surface: A club enters its second team into a stadium by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The London football club fits the sports picture, which is why 'Club' does not feel like a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Arsenal is a Premier League football club in north London.

clue.text: Love cricket club to capture trophy, an ultimately quality possession

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it prisoner, so the two letters of the club enclose the trophy and 'an'
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter counts

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A cricket club loves winning a trophy, which is a prized possession.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'trophy' and 'an' go inside the club abbreviation, splitting its two Cs.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal sense: occupancy is the holding and use of a property, a form of possession.

clue.text: Precipitous cliff alongside right-hand edge of railway — alarming

indicators.note: alongside means next to, so the two parts sit side by side
we read left to right, so a word's right-hand edge is its last letter

blocks.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

explanation.surface: A railway line runs along the edge of a sheer cliff, which is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: Scar for a cliff is a northern English word, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scary is informal for frightening, causing alarm.

clue.text: Important measures having impact, limiting female work at night

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so the impact word hems in the female letter

explanation.surface: Serious steps that restrict women working at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like employment law, with 'female work at night' as one phrase; 'female' is only an F.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the graveyard shift is the overnight stint, named for the dead quiet of the small hours.

clue.text: Old film star’s answer provided while tucking into Orvieto?

indicators.note: to tuck into food or drink is to get stuck in, so the pieces go inside the wine

blocks.note: Orvieto is an Italian white wine, so an example of vino

explanation.surface: A silent-era star answers a question while enjoying Italian wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Orvieto is a white wine from Umbria, and the question mark says it stands for wine in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Rudolph Valentino was the great romantic idol of 1920s silent films.

clue.text: Not to be swallowed, even after removing first couple of crusts

indicators.note: removing means taking out, so the named letters leave the word

blocks.note: hard to swallow means hard to believe
C and R, the first two letters of crusts, are taken out

explanation.surface: Even crusts trimmed at the edges are not fit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'Not to be swallowed' twice on purpose: a story you cannot swallow is unbelievable, and food you cannot swallow is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The literal sense: food that is not to be swallowed is unfit to eat.

clue.text: Diplomacy is hedging about means to achieve end

indicators.note: a hedge encloses a field, so the short word encloses the 'about' letter

explanation.surface: Diplomacy is a matter of evasion in pursuit of a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hedging' looks like the diplomat's evasiveness; it is a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: tactics are the planned moves used to reach a particular goal.

clue.text: Very absorbed by period leading to spring

indicators.note: one thing leading to another comes before it, so the period goes first

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly engrossed in a season that leads into spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: someone spellbound is held as if by magic, completely engrossed.

clue.text: Two were annoying about Frenchmen having moved in

indicators.note: 'about' as in 'around': the numeral goes around the Frenchmen

blocks.note: MM = Messieurs, the French plural of Mr

explanation.surface: A pair of locals complained that some Frenchmen had moved in nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' is the Roman numeral II, split so the Frenchmen can sit between its strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: to immigrate is to come into a new country to settle.

clue.text: Daring problem linked to uranium, say, on the radio

indicators.note: linked means joined, so the two sounds are run together
radio carries only sound, so what counts is how the words are said, not spelt

blocks.note: uranium is an example of a metal
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A bold radio item about a problem with uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: The uranium sound comes first in the answer though 'problem' is first in the clue, because 'linked to' allows either order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mettlesome means full of mettle, spirited and brave.

clue.text: Lots of strands and upturned components in feature of dress

indicators.note: turned upside down; in a down clue that means reading the word bottom to top

blocks.note: spaghetti is a mass of long pasta strands

explanation.surface: Many threads and upside-down pieces go into a dress design.
explanation.walkthrough: The dress picture makes 'strands' sound like thread; they are strands of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion term: a spaghetti strap is a thin shoulder strap on a dress or top.

clue.text: Where doctors work — distribute The Lancet here? Mostly

indicators.note: to distribute is to hand things out in all directions, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: anagram fodder; The Lancet is a medical journal

explanation.surface: A clinic plans to hand out copies of The Lancet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lancet is a leading British medical journal, which is why the surface feels like a doctors' waiting room.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term: a health centre is a local building housing GP surgeries and nurses.

clue.text: Excuse an ex-tutee freaking out

indicators.note: someone freaking out loses control, so the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A former pupil loses control and a teacher looks for an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'ex-tutee' is ignored; the fodder is just the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to extenuate is to lessen the seriousness of an offence, partly excusing it.

clue.text: Outcome of trial? Exiled to that place in parts of London

indicators.note: in Cockney parts of London the H is dropped from the start of words

blocks.note: HENCE, away from here, said with its H dropped

explanation.surface: The verdict: banishment to a certain district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, the speech of London's East End, drops initial H, so HENCE is said 'ENCE.

clue.text: One Greek character attached to … a burning wheel, apparently

definitions.text: One Greek character attached to … a burning wheel, apparently

blocks.note: xi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the rest of the &lit reading, adding no letters

explanation.surface: A figure of Greek myth, strapped to a flaming wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: Ixion was a Greek character bound to a burning wheel; the ellipsis marks the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue tells the myth: Zeus punished Ixion by binding him to a fiery wheel forever.

clue.text: Speculative account taking in broadcast media

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the account holds the scattered letters
to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A theoretical report about the broadcast media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast media' looks like television and radio; 'broadcast' is scattering the letters of MEDIA.

clue.text: Formalities favouring Conservative in contrivance

indicators.note: the party letter is placed in the middle of the device word

blocks.note: a tool is a device, a contrivance

explanation.surface: Official procedures that favour the Conservatives in some scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrivance' suggests a political plot; it is simply a device.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural paraphrase: protocol is the system of formal etiquette for official occasions.

clue.text: Encouraging to receive a great success in old sport

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so the encouraging word takes the success inside

blocks.note: a riot is a huge hit, as in 'the show was a riot'

explanation.surface: Spectators cheer a triumph in an ancient sport.

clue.text: Expensive rental to secure church? There are obstacles to participating in this

definitions.text: There are obstacles to participating in this

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the rental holds the church letters inside

blocks.note: a lease is a rental agreement

clue.text: Italian composer lost his grip around finale of piece

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters stray into a new order
the rearranged letters go around the final letter of piece

explanation.surface: A composer loses control near the end of a performance.

clue.text: Difficult situation, nothing less, accepted by Athenian soccer team?

blocks.note: a hole is a fix, a tight spot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing less' looks like 'no less than'; it tells you to remove the O.

clue.text: No good taking on excellent old New Zealand tree

clue.text: Surface on a sea yielding zero for lobster or similar

blocks.note: a crust is a hard surface layer
places the next piece after the crust
O, which the ocean gives up

clue.text: Examine Bill, initially lacking a certain hormone

blocks.note: a bill is a printed poster
one = a certain, as in 'one Mr Smith'

clue.text: Majestic display fed by complete source of electricity

clue.text: USA misrepresented by one in individual novel

clue.text: Tyrant upheld nonsense to support suppressing court

clue.text: Another artist included in most of Michelangelo’s work

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the shortened statue
most but not all, so the last letter goes

clue.text: A lot of fresh confusion after invasion by one deadly opponent

clue.text: Cinematic illusions in various places retaining one property

clue.text: Salesman in Florida working at top speed

clue.text: County’s attraction — cheap accommodation?

clue.text: Public meeting supporting everything except the leader

clue.text: Minute articles from the past? I don’t believe it

clue.text: Governor having message from bank being put back

clue.text: Sharpens tip of lancet, to make true
